item.title: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: President Trump told an Israeli TV network on Thursday that he is "not rushing" and could wait until 2027 to make a decision on his next move in the war with Iran. He told Fox News on Saturday that he wants a "permanent" deal with the regime. Despite Mr. Trump's remark, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new assault on Iran in the short term, with the Netanyahu administration concerned about how rapidly Iran is rebuilding its weapons production capacity.Iran on Thursday rejected Mr. Trump's accusation that it may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, with the foreign ministry saying U.S. allegations "keep changing" and are following "the same fraudulent script" as the justification for the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq.
New Updates
1:00 PM
Iran holds talks with Qatari mediators
Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks," without providing details.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran to end the war have stalled in recent months.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, however, that ongoing talks in the region must be "given a chance" and that the ongoing U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "must be lifted rationally."
"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state television.
"At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves....

item.title: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike
item.description:
Gold Star families have told CBS News that briefings about a forthcoming U.S. military report on the deadliest strike on U.S. soldiers in the Iran conflict did not, to their satisfaction, address their concerns about the military preparations and response to the attack.
Several of the families said they have been briefed about the unclassified results from the long-awaited internal probe into one of the first attacks on U.S. troops during Operation Epic Fury. Six U.S. Army Reserve soldiers were killed by a drone strike on their command post in Kuwait, known as Port Shuaiba, on March 1.
The official report has not yet been released to the public. The Pentagon has indicated it could be made public in a matter of days.
Over the past week, the Army briefed at least three Gold Star families on the investigation, and several family members told CBS News they were frustrated by what they heard.
Some of those briefed told CBS News the report does little to address the findings of an eight-month CBS News investigation, in which multiple sources said Army commanders ignored repeated warnings about the drone threat in the weeks before the attack.
Witnesses told CBS News that the facilities were not fortified to protect service members from a strike by one-way attack drones, which are a staple of the Iranian arsenal. Soldiers on the site said they had seen U.S. intelligence prior to the war showing the location was on an Iranian target list. And they argued the facilities lacked sufficient medical supplies and a plan for a mass casualty incident.
Photo obtained by CBS News shows damage from the Iranian drone attack that killed six U.S. service members in Kuwait on March 1, 2026.

item.title: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you"
item.description:
Britain's Catherine, Princess of Wales, opens up about finding hope and joy amid uncertainty in a new documentary exploring life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024.
"Heal" follows 44-year-old Catherine as she attempts the Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.
The Princess of Wales said at the time she undertook the challenge in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization connected to the hospital where she received her treatment. She was greeted by her husband Prince William, who is heir to the throne, and their children Princes George and Louis and Princess Charlotte, as well as her parents and brother after completing the climb.
In a trailer released Saturday by Prince William and Catherine's Kensington Palace office, the princess reflects on her cancer journey and speaks to others about their experiences.
Catherine, Princess of Wales, meets a cancer patient during a visit to The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust on Sept. 11, 2026, in London, England.
Ian Vogler / WPA Pool / Getty Images
Catherine announced in March 2024 that she had cancer and was undergoing chemotherapy following major abdominal surgery. She did not reveal what type of cancer she was treated for.
Catherine disclosed in January 2025 that she was in remission about 10 months after announcing her diagnosis. At the time, she said in her post on Instagram that she remains focused on recovery: "As anyone who has experienced a cancer diagnosis will know, it takes time to adjust to a new normal."
She has gradually resumed her public duties, visiting India with William earlier this month.

item.title: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer
item.description:
Catherine, the Princess of Wales, said Tuesday her cancer is in remission, about 10 months after announcing her diagnosis. Princess Kate made the announcement on social media after visiting the London hospital where she received treatment.
"It is a relief to now be in remission and I remain focused on recovery," she said in her post on Instagram after visiting the Royal Marsden Hospital in London. "As anyone who has experienced a cancer diagnosis will know, it takes time to adjust to a new normal."
The princess had announced last March that cancer was discovered following an abdominal surgery and she was undergoing preventative chemotherapy.
In September, she said she had finished chemotherapy. She spoke about receiving the cancer treatment during her visit Tuesday. "It's really tough,'' she said, according to the Associated Press. "It's such a shock."
Kate spoke with patient Katherine Field about the chemotherapy port that's used to deliver the treatment, saying, "I got so attached to it," and joking that she was almost reluctant to have it removed, according to the AP.
Catherine, Princess of Wales, talks with Katherine Field as she visits The Royal Marsden hospital on Jan. 14, 2025, in London.
Chris Jackson/Pool via Reuters
On social media Tuesday, Kate said she visited the hospital to thank the staff "for looking after me so well during the past year."
"My heartfelt thanks goes to all those who have quietly walked alongside William and me as we have navigated everything," she said, referring to her husband, the Prince of Wales. "We couldn't have asked for more. The care and advice we have received throughout my time as a patient has been exceptional."

item.title: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI
item.description:
Mexico's military announced Saturday that it had captured a drug kingpin on the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Top 10 Most Wanted List. Violence broke out in the state of Sinaloa afterwards, rattling civilians.
Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, also known as "El Chapo Isidro," is allegedly the leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, which the FBI described as a "heavily armed, major drug-trafficking organization" based in Sinaloa.
The cartel is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution and importation of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the U.S., according to the FBI, and has controlled drug production, transportation and distribution throughout Mexico.
Meza-Flores and two other leaders of the organization were captured by special forces during a raid in Sinaloa on Friday night, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X.
Elite military agents were able to find the targets, then arrive surreptitiously in the area, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said. The agents set perimeters around a residence to prevent Meza-Flores from escaping, while also defending the area from reinforcements who could have interrupted the operation.
The arresting agents were attacked with gunfire and explosives, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said. The agents entered the house and captured Meza-Flores and the two others. The three were then evacuated to Mexico City and placed in custody.
Video shared by authorities shows heavily armed men in camouflage marching a man who appeared to be Meza Flores through a dimly lit house and putting him in the back of a truck.

item.title: Denmark says Russia behind plot to kill U.S.-Ukrainian citizen on its soil
item.description:
Authorities in Denmark thwarted an attempted assassination of an American Ukrainian rapper on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, officials said Friday.
Officials said Friday that police thwarted the attempt when they arrested three men with links to the Danish criminal underworld in a car before the rapper Kyivstoner was set to perform at a concert north of Copenhagen in late September.
According to the Danish PET intelligence agency, a search of the vehicle uncovered firearms and knives.
Two people were placed under formal investigation on Friday for attempted murder and for assisting a foreign intelligence service in its operations within Denmark.
Police and the intelligence services suspect Loyal to Familia, a Danish street gang and criminal network, of having taken part in the planning of the hit.
"A Russian assassination attempt is not something we've seen in Denmark before, and that gives me an impression of an increasingly aggressive and risk-taking Russia," Kieffer-Kristensen told the press conference. "We believe that the case is important for understanding the threat that Denmark faces from Russia."
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called the alleged plot "a clear illustration of the serious security situation in which Denmark and Europe find themselves."
"We are facing a cornered Russia, acting more aggressively and with a greater propensity to take risks," she said in a statement.
Soon after the announcement, Denmark's foreign minister said Denmark will expel Russia's defense attaché in Copenhagen in response.
"We don't want to break off diplomatic relations with Russia in this particular situation that Denmark and Europe are in... But on the other hand, we want to send a very, very strong signal," Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said, calling the alleged plot an unacceptable transgression.
